comp_011:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up the recurring board meeting cadence using {{vendor}}, our scheduling tool. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have them, ask me for: the desired board meeting frequency (e.g., quarterly, monthly), preferred day/time window, meeting duration, the list of board member emails (or confirm you should pull them from an existing contacts/calendar list), and which calendars (Google, Outlook, Apple) should be connected for conflict-checking.
2. Using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}, check availability across all connected calendars for the proposed cadence and identify a recurring slot that avoids conflicts for all board members.
3. Create an availability schedule for the board cadence (working hours, any known out-of-office periods) if {{vendor}} supports this.
4. Set up the recurring board meeting as a bookable event/booking in {{vendor}}, using the operations exposed via {{vendor}}'s API or tool-calling/MCP surface — do this end to end without requiring me to use the dashboard, if that capability exists.
5. Confirm the recurring booking is created correctly (correct cadence, correct attendees, correct calendar sync) and that it appears on all board members' connected calendars.
6. If rescheduling or cancellation is needed at any point, use the same API/tool-calling surface rather than asking me to do it manually.

Done looks like: a confirmed recurring board meeting series exists in {{vendor}}, synced across all relevant calendars, with the correct cadence, duration, and attendee list, and no double-booking conflicts.

Report back with: the cadence and time slot chosen, the list of attendees included, confirmation the recurring booking was created successfully, and any conflicts or issues you encountered that need my input.

comp_011:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a reusable board meeting minutes template inside {{vendor}}, our project-management tool, as part of our board minutes cadence process. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization name or URL, (2) the project or space where board materials should live (or whether to create a new one), and (3) any prior minutes or a standard agenda structure I want reflected (e.g. attendance, prior minutes approval, officer/committee reports, motions & votes, action items, adjournment).

Once you have this, do the following in {{vendor}}:
1. Check whether {{vendor}} offers a pre-built meeting minutes or board minutes template; if so, use it as the starting point. If not, create a new shared document from scratch.
2. Structure the template with clearly labeled sections: meeting metadata (date, time, location/method), attendees and quorum confirmation, approval of prior minutes, reports, discussion items, motions with proposer/seconder and vote outcome, action items with owners and due dates, and adjournment time.
3. Organize the document within a dedicated project or folder for board governance so it sits alongside related board materials, and name it clearly (e.g. "Board Minutes Template").
4. Add placeholder text or brackets where meeting-specific details will be filled in later, so the template can be duplicated for each meeting.

Done looks like: a clearly organized, reusable minutes template exists in {{vendor}}, is stored in the correct board-governance project/folder, and is ready to be duplicated and filled in for the next scheduled board meeting.

Report back with: the location/link of the template, a summary of the sections included, and confirmation that it's saved in the correct project space.

comp_011:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for an upcoming board meeting, since holding the meeting and deliberating remains a human step that you cannot perform. Please prepare all the supporting materials so the meeting itself runs smoothly and the minutes are captured correctly afterward.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the meeting date/time, the agenda items, the list of directors and any invited officers/observers, the minutes template location (e.g., in our data room or document storage), the prior meeting's minutes for reference, and any resolutions or matters requiring a vote.

Then do the following:
1. Draft a clean meeting agenda from the items I give you, in standard board format (call to order, approval of prior minutes, reports, old/new business, action items, adjournment).
2. Pre-fill the minutes template with the date, time, location/platform, attendee list, and agenda structure, leaving blank fields for actual discussion notes, motions, seconds, and vote tallies to be filled in live during the meeting.
3. Prepare a short pre-meeting checklist for me: confirm quorum, confirm dial-in/room logistics, distribute the agenda and any board materials in advance, and identify who will serve as minute-taker.
4. If a video conferencing or recording tool is already part of our workflow, note where the recording/transcript would be saved for later reference, but do not attempt to convene or run the meeting yourself.

When finished, give me: the drafted agenda, the pre-filled minutes template, and the pre-meeting checklist, clearly labeled and ready for use. Note explicitly that convening the meeting, facilitating discussion, calling votes, and recording real-time minutes remains a human step — you are only preparing the materials, not conducting the meeting.

comp_011:n4.prompt:
You are helping me circulate the latest board meeting minutes for signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature tool. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the finalized minutes document (or its location), the list of board member/signatory names and emails, the desired signing order (if sequential), and any deadline/expiration date for signatures.
2. Using your configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and create a new signature request, uploading the minutes document.
3. Configure the routing: add each signer in the correct order (sequential or parallel, per my instructions), set an expiration date, and enable automatic reminders for outstanding signatures.
4. Verify all signature fields (or initials/date fields) are correctly placed on the document — reposition or add any missing fields as needed.
5. Prepare a summary showing: the signer list and order, expiration date, reminder cadence, and a preview or confirmation that the document and fields are correctly set up.
6. Do NOT send the signature request yet. Since this step requires explicit human approval before changes are applied, present the fully prepared request (signers, order, expiration, reminders, field placement) to me for review and stop for human sign-off.

Once I confirm the setup is correct and give explicit approval, you may proceed to send the request through {{vendor}}. Until then, do not click send, submit, or finalize anything on my behalf.

When reporting back, include: the document name/version routed, the full signer list with order, the expiration date, reminder settings, and a link or reference to the draft request in {{vendor}} for my review.

comp_011:n5.prompt:
You are helping me file signed board minutes into our corporate data room. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the location/path of the fully executed (signed) minutes file, the meeting date it corresponds to, and which data room service we use (for example Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, or a dedicated data room tool) plus confirmation that you have access via my configured credentials.

2. Locate the correct destination folder in the data room — typically a structure like Board Materials > Minutes > [Year], or wherever prior board minutes are already filed. If no such folder exists, create one following the existing naming and folder convention.

3. Upload the signed minutes file to that folder. Name the file consistently with prior filings (e.g., "YYYY-MM-DD Board Minutes - Signed.pdf"). If a draft or unsigned version already exists in the data room, replace or clearly supersede it, keeping a version history if the platform supports it.

4. Set appropriate access permissions on the file consistent with how prior board minutes are shared (e.g., restricted to board members/officers), matching existing data room permission conventions rather than inventing new ones.

5. Verify the upload succeeded: confirm the file opens correctly, is legible, and is placed in the right folder with the right name and permissions.

When done, report back to me with: the exact file path/location in the data room, the filename used, the permissions applied, and confirmation that the file was verified as legible and correctly signed. If you cannot access the data room or locate the signed file, stop and tell me exactly what is missing rather than guessing at folder structure or credentials.
